question: Does Hexyl's empty-input special row use a different panel geometry from the surrounding border in binary base mode?

sources.name: sharkdp/hexyl
sources.claim: Binary base uses wider per-byte digit geometry and can auto-select one panel, while Printer::print_all handles empty input with fixed No content row separators rather than deriving all cells from self.panels.

sources.name: hexyl issue 288
sources.claim: Binary-base output for an empty file is reported to render a broken table while other bases remain aligned.

command: GitHub Actions: Fieldwork Hexyl empty binary geometry probe

dependencies: exact sharkdp/hexyl source fetched read-only at 6ecc29b9c8c84d08a7e860f7f69c22b113b480ea

distinguishing_outcomes.observation: Stripped binary empty output has the same display width on every table row, matching the hexadecimal control.
distinguishing_outcomes.interpretation: Current source no longer reproduces the reported geometry mismatch; retain a negative result.

distinguishing_outcomes.observation: Hexadecimal empty output is row-width consistent while binary empty output contains a No content row whose width differs from its border rows.
distinguishing_outcomes.interpretation: The special empty-input owner has a target-executed panel-geometry mismatch specific to the binary one-panel layout.

target_execution.result: With fixed terminal width 80 and an empty file, hexadecimal output rows are 80,80,80. Binary output rows are 45,80,45: the one-panel border is 45 columns while the No content row retains the fixed two-panel geometry.

stop_condition: Promoted after exact target CLI reproduction. Continue source work only in a Fieldwork candidate carrier or owned Hexyl fork; refresh overlap before any external proposal.
